title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR stands in for Charles Martel — a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours, and a completely different polity
SALADIN stands in for Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi — an Ayyubid Kurdish sultan of the 1180s from Egypt/Syria, not an 8th-century Umayyad governor of al-Andalus
EL_CID stands in for Duke Odo of Aquitaine — a Castilian magnate of the 1090s, wrong century and wrong realm
CROSSBOWMAN x2 in the Frankish roster: the crossbow was not a battlefield arm of Carolingian Francia in 732
PIKEMAN x4 for the Frankish shield wall: the massed pike is a 14th-century development; SPEARMAN/MILITIA-line would have been the period-appropriate engine choice
KNIGHT x9 as the core of the Umayyad army — the fully-armoured Frankish-style knight is a poor stand-in when the engine offers LIGHT_CAVALRY/CAMEL_RIDER and Saracen-style raiders

MONASTERY in the Frankish camp is a generic Western European chapel building rather than anything tied to the 732 field position, and El Cid's STABLE for the Aquitanians duplicates the Umayyad cavalry theme

issues_found: Charles Martel is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero unit — a named figure from 1066, three centuries later. The engine has no Martel hero, but a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic/Frankish infantry hero stand-in was available, so this is avoidable error.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN, a named 12th-century Ayyubid sultan; the victory condition literally reads 'DESTROY_OBJECT on SALADIN'.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian figure — and one associated with the opposing (Iberian/Muslim-adjacent) side, compounding the confusion.

Both active players are set to civilization RANDOM, so Frankish and Umayyad architecture, unit availability, and bonuses are left to chance rather than assigned (Franks and Saracens/Berbers were all available).

Player 3 (the Aquitanians, nominally Frankish allies) is a purely cavalry force (6 Knights, 4 Scout Cavalry) with a Stable, while the Umayyad player fields Knights rather than any Frankish-side counterpart — the visual distinction between the sides is muddled.

Player 1's roster includes an ARCHERY_RANGE, CROSSBOWMAN x2 and a MONASTERY — crossbows are several centuries premature for an 8th-century Frankish host, and there is no reason to place them when spearmen/champions already carry the shield-wall role.
5,306 oak trees on a 120x120 map is a blunt-instrument representation of 'wooded high ground'; no elevation or terrain differentiation is evident from the placed content.
Force scale is tiny (roughly 17 Frankish and 16 Umayyad combatants) for an engagement of this reputation.

Charles Martel is represented by the WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR hero — a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours; a renamed generic Champion or Teutonic-style infantry hero was available and would have been correct.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is represented by SALADIN — a late-12th-century Kurdish Ayyubid sultan, wrong dynasty, wrong region and wrong era for an 8th-century Umayyad wali of al-Andalus.
Duke Odo of Aquitaine is represented by EL_CID — an 11th-century Castilian, again the wrong person and century.
Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Frankish and Andalusian architecture and unit sets are left to chance rather than assigned (Franks and Saracens/Berbers were both available).
Player 2's Umayyad force fields CAMEL_RIDER units; the Andalusian army at Tours was overwhelmingly horse cavalry, and the engine's Knight/Light Cavalry mix already covered it.
The 'hidden Aquitanians under Odo who must be rallied by a messenger' is an invention — Odo's forces were already operating with Charles, not concealed off-map awaiting a signal.
Force scale is very thin (17 Frankish and 16 Umayyad combatants) for an engagement described as repeated mass cavalry charges against a shield wall.
The 'ford' the cavalry crosses in the narration is not represented by any terrain or water feature in the placed objects.
